name: Juan Gil de Hontañón
summary:
Juan Gil de Hontañón was a master builder and Trasmeran mason of Spain during the 16th century. He worked in the royal court of King Philip II, producing some of his most renowned works, including the Isabelline Gothic Segovia Cathedral, which took over three decades to complete.

Hontañón was a key figure in the development of Spanish Renaissance architecture, drawing inspiration from classical models while incorporating local elements. His innovative use of brickwork and ornate details influenced architects across Europe.

The master builder's legacy can be seen in numerous monuments throughout Spain, including the Castle of Turégano, El Parral Monastery, and the Cathedral of Palencia. His contributions to Spanish architecture have left a lasting impact on the country's cultural heritage.

"The mastery of Hontañón is not only reflected in his own works but also in those of his contemporaries, who followed his lead and pushed the boundaries of architectural expression."
